newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Smelter woes weigh on WMC nickel output.
newsitem.headline: Smelter woes weigh on WMC nickel output.

text.p: Production of nickel metal and matte by Australian mining house WMC Ltd suffered in 1996/97 (July/June) due to an accident at its Kalgoorlie smelter in April, WMC said on Wednesday.
Production of nickel metal fell 17.5 percent to 9,027 tonnes in the quarter to June 30 versus the previous quarter, it said.
Output of nickel matte over the same period declined 34.3 percent to 13,122 tonnes, WMC said.
"This shutdown had a significant effect on the nickel matte and metal production and an adverse impact on unit costs for 1996/97," WMC said.
On April 6, part of the flash furnace at the smelter collapsed, leading to a 41-day shutdown.
In 1996/97, nickel metal production increased slightly to 47,577 tonnes from 46,712 in the previous year while production of nickel in matte form fell to 72,939 tonnes from 77,316.
In its other main commodities, WMC recorded mostly slight gains in June quarter production over the previous quarter.

Alumina output by The Alcoa World Alumina joint venture, 60-40 owned by Aluminum Co of America and WMC, rose 1.6 percent to 2.6 million tonnes for the quarter, increasing full year output to 10 million tonnes, WMC said
The quarterly increase reflected a higher operating target to meet an increasing demand for alumina, the company said.
Gold output for the quarter was 233,170 ounces, up 2.9 percent over the march quarter while full year gold production totalled 832,000 ounces, up 3.5 precent on 1995/96.

WMC also said it was deferring a A$157 million expansion of its St Ives gold mine in Western Australia because of low gold prices. The expansion was to eventually lift St Ives production to 700,000 ounces a year from the current 400,000 ounces.

Uranium oxide concentrate production from the Olympic Dam mine in South Australia for the June quarter totalled 405 tonnes, taking 1996/97 output to 1,758 tonnes from 1,652 tonnes in the previous year.
Silver output, also from Olympic Dam, totalled 85,172 ounces in the June quarter, bringing full year silver production to 346,882 ounces, down from 381,479 ounces in 1995/96, WMC's figures show.
